claims.explanation: TW-37 is a BH3-mimetic that binds BCL2, BCL-XL, and MCL1, so selectivity likely reflects which anti-apoptotic BCL2-family proteins the tumor depends on for survival. Lines with intact apoptosis signaling and dependence on BCL2/MCL1 (e.g., TP53-mutant, KRAS-mutant pancreatic/gastric/esophageal tumors) are sensitized, whereas lines with alternative survival signaling or low BCL2-family dependence are protected.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with loss of p53-mediated apoptosis resistance
TW-37 binds MCL1 with high affinity; MCL1-dependent tumors are expected to be killed
TW-37 was designed to target the BCL2 BH3-binding groove
TW-37 binds BCL-XL and BCL-XL can mediate sensitivity in some lineages
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven MCL1 dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are among the most killed, consistent with MAPK-pathway dependence on MCL1
PTEN-mutant lines are enriched in the least-affected set, suggesting PI3K/AKT survival signaling compensates
EGFR-mutant lung lines are among the least affected, indicating EGFR-driven survival bypasses BCL2-family inhibition
SF3B1-mutant lines appear in both sets but are enriched in the least-affected group
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with sensitive melanoma and bone lines, possibly reflecting apoptotic priming
NF1-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set, consistent with RAS-pathway activation and MCL1 dependence
ATM-mutant lines are present in the least-affected set, suggesting altered DNA-damage/apoptotic signaling
